chunks: When they are told: "Spend of what God has given you," the unbelievers say to those who believe: "Why should we feed those whom God should have fed if He pleased?" You are only in palpable error.
ai.seo_question: What is the argument of the disbelievers regarding charity and divine decree?
ai.summary: In Surah Yaseen, this verse highlights the arrogance of the disbelievers who used divine predestination (Qadr) as an excuse to neglect their duty of charity (Sadaqah), claiming God would feed the poor directly if He willed. Shia scholars, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, emphasize that this reasoning reflects a misunderstanding of the interplay between divine will and human agency, where God's decree is often realized through human action. The verse serves as a critique of passive fatalism, urging believers to actively participate in social welfare as a manifestation of God's mercy.
